title: Local Muscle Vibration for Muscle Strength and Walking in Individuals With Chronic Ankle Instability
official: Effects of Local Muscle Vibration on Evertor Muscle Strength and Gait Biomechanics in Individuals With Chronic Ankle Instability
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether local muscle vibration improves ankle muscle strength in people with chronic ankle instability. The study will also examine whether local muscle vibration changes the way people walk and whether changes in muscle strength are related to balance, ankle awareness, and previous ankle injuries.

The main questions are:

* Does local muscle vibration increase ankle muscle strength compared with no treatment?
* Does local muscle vibration change the way people walk compared with no treatment?
* Are changes in muscle strength after local muscle vibration related to balance, sensation, ankle awareness, and previous ankle injuries?

Participants will:

* Complete assessments of ankle strength, walking, balance, and ankle awareness
* Complete two treatment sessions on separate days, in random order: one with local muscle vibration and one with no treatment
* Complete ankle muscle strength and walking assessments before and after each session
* Walk on a treadmill while their movements and the forces under their feet are recorded
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age between 18- 35 years.
* Have at least two self-reported lateral ankle sprains at any point in time.
* Have experienced at least one episode of giving way within the past six months.
* Score ≥11 on the Identification of Functional Ankle Instability questionnaire.
* Score \<90 on The Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) and \<80 on FAAM-sport questionnaires.
* Being Physically active.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unable to read or speak English.
* Age younger than 18 or older than 35 years.
* A history of an acute lateral ankle sprain within the past four weeks.
* A history of lower extremity surgery or major ligamentous injury (e.g., torn ACL).
* Presence of balance disorders.
* Being Physically Inactive.
* A concussion or head injury in the past six months.
* A history of cardiovascular conditions or stroke.
* Currently pregnant (based on self-report).
